featured_reviews.review_text:
Service: The place is hygienic and clean given the food and well placed. The service is good although they sometimes get flustered when there are multiple customers.

Food: There are a wide variety of bakery products including cakes, pastries, breads, cookies, puffs, tea time bakes. They are mostly well prepared and cost friendly. The Cream Roll needs more cream as the bottom of the roll is just biscuit and no cream.

Recommendations: Try their Apple Pie (add vanilla ice cream to enhance the flavours) it is full of flavours and well made. The Khari and Butter are great bites with tea and coffee. The Pista Cookies are their highlight! They are soft and full of dry fruits and fresh!

featured_reviews.name: Sonam Pawar - Nucleus Technologies
featured_reviews.review_text:
Edward Bakery, nestled in the heart of Fort on Perin Nariman Street, Borabazar Precinct, is a charming old-world gem that has been serving its patrons for an impressive 90 years. This historic bakery is a must-visit if you're in the Ballard Estate area.

Food Quality:
Edward Bakery is renowned for its wide range of freshly baked goods, all prepared in-house with great care and attention to detail. The quality of their products is exceptional, with everything tasting fresh and flavorful. The highlight of their menu is the Puffs, which are a must-try. These are flaky, buttery, and filled with deliciousness—truly one of the best puffs you'll find in Mumbai.

Ambience & Service:
The bakery exudes an old-world charm with its classic interiors, reminding you of the rich heritage and history it carries. The staff are friendly and efficient, ensuring you have a pleasant experience whether you're picking up a quick snack or browsing through their selection.

Overall Experience:
Edward Bakery is more than just a place to grab a bite—it's a slice of Mumbai's culinary history. Whether you're in the mood for their famous puffs, freshly baked bread, or a variety of other bakery items, you won't be disappointed. The consistent quality and freshness of their offerings make it a beloved spot for both locals and visitors alike.

If you're in Fort, make sure to stop by Edward Bakery for a taste of tradition and some truly delicious treats!

featured_reviews.name: Aditya Bharsake
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Sassanian feels like walking into a time capsule aged tiles, vintage mirrors, and that unmistakable old-world Irani café charm. You can almost picture Bollywood legends sipping chai here once upon a time.

Now let’s talk food;
Mawa Cake: Soft and nostalgic, though slightly underwhelming on flavor. Still, it has that old-school appeal. 3.5/5

Bread Pudding: Sadly didn’t live up to the legacy. A bit too soggy and bland for our taste. 2/5

Caramel Pudding: Smooth and sweet, but lacked that rich, caramel depth. Still a decent pick if you love simple desserts. 3/5

Bhurji Pav: Star of the show! Perfectly spiced, comforting, and a total mood. Highly recommend.

Veg Puff: Stuffing was tasty, but the outer pastry felt oily; could use some refinement. Friend said the chicken puff was "just okay" too.

Spent ₹400 for 2, Value for money considering the ambiance and legacy.

Overall: 3/5
Would I go again? Maybe not for the food, but absolutely for the experience. The café has character, history, and a charm that’s fading in today’s fast-food era. Come for the vibe, order the bhurji pav, soak in the nostalgia, and take a moment to slow down.

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text: I discovered this amazing bakery purely by accident during a casual stroll on lunch break. It is located a leisurely 10 mins walk from the CST railway station. I believe it is a Parsi managed bakery which is expected with almost all of the famous eateries, bakeries and cafés in the Ballard estate and Fort area. The bakery itself looks so inviting and has a nice clean decor and it stands out even more in comparison to the rather u assuming shops and restaurants around it. The egg and non-egg containing baked stuff is clearly labelled so you don’t have to ask. The mix and f the sweet and savoury stuff is perfect. In fact, you may as well have the savouries here which again has an excellent selection of vegetarian and non-vegetarian choices that are clearly labelled and you can literally end the meal with their assortment of pastries, puffs - sweet stuff and was it down with the signature Bombay soda they offer in desi flavours like kala khatta, masala lime, mango and other flavours. I particularly would recommend the classic cream puff and the caramel cream puff which is a small slice of heaven. The kala khatta soda is also really good. I have not tried the savoury stuff yet and hope to one of these days. The only let down is the Irani chai which I personally did not like because it has too much milk (it’s a personal choice and nothing to do with Irani chai per se). But what I certainly did not like is that the Irani chai is prepared beforehand and chilled in a refrigerator and then heated in a microwave and served on demand. In India, we like our tea piping hot right off the stove not reheated. Aside this minor dislike, it’s really a great bakery and very reasonably priced too. I hope they open more of their stores in the suburbs too.

featured_reviews.name: Review Man
featured_reviews.review_text:
Harley’s Ivory Lounge

We walked into Harley’s Ivory Lounge at Kala Ghoda with two things guiding us. The almost unbelievable 4.8 rating across thousands of reviews and the dreamy photographs online that promised a café from another world. The approach did little to prepare us, for the street outside was dim and unremarkable, almost post-apocalyptic in its neglect. And then suddenly the café appeared, glowing like a castle from a fairytale, standing proud in the middle of ruin. Inside, the spell continued. It was heavenly in its beauty, every corner carefully crafted. The only slip was the use of AI art in some frames, which felt more tacky than tasteful, but beyond that it was a space that held you. The booths were elegant, the plating was charming, and the staff carried the same grace, explaining the menu patiently when it seemed unfamiliar. It felt like a refuge, especially for those who wander Kala Ghoda late into the night, since the doors stay open till midnight.

The food began with the pistachio medovik, the Russian honey cake that arrived layered like a poem. The pistachio sang most in the top layer, while the cream in between was rich and perhaps too thick, and the lower bread base leaned towards crumbly. Yet it was still a dish of substance, one that lingered on the tongue. Alongside came a lemon macaron, delicate on the outside, but the filling inside leaned harder than perfection would demand. The attempt was admirable, the execution almost there. The choco medovik hot chocolate was an indulgence, large in portion, flecked with medovik pieces, sweet and satisfying but tilting into cloying by the end. Its texture was smooth but not as luxuriously thick as some of the best, and perhaps a smaller, denser version would balance price and pleasure better. The small cube of medovik served alongside was a thoughtful touch, though in the company of so many sweets it became a test of endurance.

In the end, Harley’s Ivory Lounge dazzled us. The ambience was extraordinary, the staff warm, the plating memorable. The food had its strengths and its stumbles, but wrapped within such a setting, the flaws softened. Looking back, perhaps the ambience is carrying much of the weight of that near perfect rating. Still, it remains a place to which one would happily return, if only to try its savoury secrets and sit once more in a castle that rises out of nowhere.

8/10

One sip of their 7-layer Choco Medovik hot chocolate, and you immediately notice the finesse and thought behind every detail.

From beautifully curated festive gifting hampers and gift sets to Russian Medovik cakes, indulgent cheesecakes, delicate French macarons, along with a comforting coffee and food menu featuring pizzas, croissant sandwiches, and more, there’s something here for every festive craving.

Adding to its legacy, the cafe has also won a Guinness World Record for creating the World’s Largest Medovik Cake.

Choosing favourites wasn’t easy, but the Pistachio Delights and Lotus Biscoff Medovik are absolute must-tries.

📍 Located in Fort, Kala Ghoda, just a one-minute walk from BSE Mumbai, this place is definitely a must-visit, especially during the festive season.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’d always wanted to visit one of the oldest bakeries in town ,Kyani & Co.and finally got the chance. The ambience is wonderfully nostalgic, filled with old-school charm, and I absolutely loved that part of the experience.

However, the food didn’t quite live up to the hype. The dishes we tried, like the kheema and bhurji, felt quite basic and nothing exceptional. On the brighter side, the snack items were much better , the mawa cake, chicken cutlet, and ,caramel custard were genuinely enjoyable.

Overall, the pricing is reasonable, making it worth a visit for the ambience and certain snacks, but don’t expect too much from the main dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kyani & Co. is a classic Iranian café serving authentic Iranian cuisine. The place is always crowded, and you’ll notice a good mix of locals and foreigners, which shows how popular and well-known it is.

Coming to the food, their chicken dishes stood out. The Chicken Cheese Kebab was actually very nice—it was stuffed with cheese from inside and had a hot-dog–like shape. It felt filling and had a good amount of chicken, which I liked the most.

I also tried the chicken samosa, but I felt the chicken quantity was a bit less, with more masala in the filling. Similarly, the mutton cutlet had more potato than mutton. Personally, I prefer meat-forward dishes.

The ambience is really great with an old-world charm, but photography is not allowed inside. I clicked one photo and was asked not to take pictures, which was a bit disappointing considering how beautiful the place is.

Overall, it’s an authentic Iranian café with a lovely atmosphere. The food is good, especially the chicken items, though the filling ratios may not suit everyone’s taste.

featured_reviews.name: Viraj Redkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Kyani & Co. and honestly, it felt less like a café visit and more like a journey back in time. The moment you walk in, the old-world charm hits you — vintage wooden furniture, classic tiled floors, and an atmosphere that carries stories from over 100 years ago. It’s raw, real, and beautifully untouched.
We ordered the iconic Irani chai, bun maska, and kheema pav — and every bite was pure nostalgia. The chai had that perfect strong, comforting flavor, the bun maska was soft with just the right amount of buttery goodness, and the kheema pav was rich, flavorful, and absolutely satisfying.
What makes this place special isn’t just the food — it’s the experience. No fancy frills, no modern distractions, just timeless simplicity done right.
A small heads-up: it’s strictly cash only — no cards, no UPI — which somehow adds to its old-school vibe.
If you’re in Mumbai and want to experience something authentic, soulful, and truly fascinating, this place is not just a café… it’s a legacy you can taste.

featured_reviews.name: Sourajyoti
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazdani Bakery is one of those places in Mumbai that feels frozen in time. Started in 1953, it has been run by the same family for generations and still carries the old Irani café charm. The bakery is located in an old heritage building near Fort and Colaba, and the moment you step inside, you feel like you’ve walked into a different era — with its wooden furniture, old photographs, and simple, no-nonsense setup.
Yazdani is best known for its brun maska (soft bun with butter) and Irani chai, which is probably the most popular order here. Their mawa cake is legendary — rich, soft and full of flavour — and often sells out quickly. Other favourites include khari biscuits, apple pie, plum cake, and freshly baked breads and cookies. Everything tastes homemade and fresh, which is what keeps people coming back.
The place is not fancy, and service is simple, but that’s part of its charm. You come here not for luxury, but for nostalgia, honest food, and a slice of old Bombay. If you want to experience Mumbai’s Irani café culture and enjoy some classic bakery items, Yazdani is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Yazdani Bakery Takeaway: A Taste of Nostalgia
Yazdani Bakery is more than just a place to grab a bite; it's a living monument to Mumbai’s Irani cafe heritage. Opting for a takeaway from this institution is a smart choice for those eager to savor its legendary bakes without the old-school dine-in experience (currently limited anyway).
The magic lies in the Brun Maska—a crusty, yet tender, bread generously slathered with creamy butter—and the dense, aromatic Mawa Cake. These staples are impeccably fresh, a testament to the bakery's commitment to quality ingredients and traditional wood-fire ovens. Don't overlook the Shrewsbury Biscuits or the flaky, savory Khari. Packaging is basic and efficient—perfectly functional for transport.
While the interior retains a charmingly worn, antique aesthetic, the focus here is the edible legacy. The staff can occasionally be brisk, but the efficiency ensures a quick transaction. A Yazdani takeaway isn't just buying baked goods; it's securing a comforting, consistent piece of culinary history to enjoy in your own space. It's an indispensable, buttery, sweet slice of Mumbai.

Walking into this bakery always feels comforting—familiar aromas, shelves full of freshly baked goodness, and the assurance that you’ll walk out with something you’ll genuinely enjoy. Theobroma Bakery has built that kind of trust over time, especially for those who value quality over gimmicks.

Their fresh sourdough and artisanal breads are absolute standouts and personal favourites—beautifully crusted, well-fermented, and full of character. The quiches and tarts are consistently satisfying, with buttery bases and well-balanced fillings that make them reliable picks every time. The tea cakes are another strong point: soft, moist, and understated, making them perfect companions to coffee or tea.

The pastry and cake counter is equally impressive, offering a wide range of flavours—from indulgent chocolate classics to lighter, nuanced options. Each dessert feels thoughtfully made, never overly sweet, and always well-executed. What’s equally commendable is the good balance of savoury items, which adds depth to the menu and keeps things interesting beyond desserts.

It’s the kind of place you return to not just for cravings, but for consistency, comfort, and the quiet joy of well-made food.

featured_reviews.name: Arin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Markiv’s feels like a café that knows exactly what it wants to be and stays within that comfort zone. It offers a fairly extensive menu of continental and café-style dishes, presented neatly and priced in the mid-range for the area.

We tried the Americano, Peach Iced Tea, Grilled Chicken Risotto, and Chicken Markiv’s.

The Americano was straightforward and clean, no bitterness, no complexity. It does what an Americano is expected to do, without leaving a strong impression either way. The Peach Iced Tea was refreshing and mildly sweet, pleasant enough for Mumbai weather, though not particularly memorable.

The Chicken Risotto was decent. Creamy, adequately cooked, and comforting, but lacked depth or a distinct flavour punch. It felt safe rather than inspired. A good option if you’re in the mood for something mild and filling, but not something you’d crave or remember later.

The Chicken Markiv’s, which appears to be one of their signature dishes, was served well and plated nicely. The chicken was tender and paired with mashed potatoes and vegetables. Again, the flavours were balanced and acceptable, but it didn’t rise above being just fine. Nothing was wrong with the dish, but nothing truly stood out either.

The menu itself is broad, covering pizzas, burgers, pasta, risottos, rice plates, and main course options, both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. It caters well to mixed groups with varied preferences. Portions are reasonable, and pricing is what you’d expect from a café of this type.

Service was polite and timely, without being overly warm or inattentive. The ambience is comfortable and casual, suitable for conversations, short meetings, or a relaxed meal, though it doesn’t have a distinct character that sets it apart from similar cafés.

Overall, Cafe Markiv’s is reliable but unremarkable. Nothing great, nothing bad. It’s a decent place if you’re nearby and want a predictable café meal without surprises. Not a destination café, but functional and consistent for what it offers.

featured_reviews.name: Zaina
featured_reviews.review_text:
The ambiance is cozy with beautifully displayed desserts that instantly catch your eye and make the place feel warm and inviting.

"Desserts are the real heroes here".
The Sebastian Cake is a must-try and the custard Bombolini is dangerously good.
Cakes, pastries and cookies are all fresh and worth picking up for takeaway.
The staff are polite and always happy to help. The only downside is the service coordination. One person takes the order, another asks what you ordered, someone else brings the food and a different person arrives with the bill. By the end you're not sure who your server actually is. 😅 Better coordination would make the experience much smoother.

Food Ratings:
•Sebastian Cake – 5/5
•French Vanilla Bombolini – 5/5
•Cookies – 4/5
•Pastries & Cakes – 4/5
•Chicken nuggets - 4/5
•Veg Russian Sandwich - 4/5
•Pani Puri – 3/5
•Sev Puri – 2/5
•Italian Pizza – 1/5
•French Fries - 1/5
The French fries were excessively crisp and hard to the point where they became uncomfortable to eat after a few bites. A slightly lighter fry would improve them considerably.

Bottom Line : Come for the desserts, stay for the desserts and probably order more desserts.
The bakery section shines far brighter than the savoury menu.

featured_reviews.name: Bilal Tajak
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today, we went to Deliure around 8:00 PM and placed our order. The staff told us it would take 40–45 minutes. Despite the long delay, we waited patiently as we are regular customers. While we were sitting inside, a major parking issue was unfolding outside. It was entirely Deliure’s fault because they failed to arrange proper parking management, which caused a lot of trouble for the locals and led to a massive traffic jam. Consequently, people complained to the police. The local police and traffic police arrived at the scene and took two of Deliure's managers to the police station.
When we finally walked outside, we found that our vehicle had been fined. This happened even though we had parked our vehicle exactly where the Deliure staff had instructed us to. When we went back inside to confront the Deliure management about this, they bluntly told us that they were not responsible for the fine, and their behaviour towards us was extremely rude.
They could have easily informed us about the ongoing parking issue with the police while we were waiting inside for our order, and they could have asked us to move our vehicle. However, they chose not to do so, and because of their negligence, we ended up with a fine. Do we really deserve this treatment? We waited so long for our food, and in return, we had to pay a fine! Is this how they respect their regular customers?
Furthermore, this entire parking chaos and heavy order load escalated because Deliure was prioritizing online orders over offline walk-in customers. Their mentality is crystal clear—they only care about making money from online orders, making offline customers wait indefinitely, and leaving them in deep trouble when their vehicles get fined due to the establishment's mismanagement.
